verdicts.claim: PASSIVE mode copies as many WAL frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers, and never invokes the busy-handler callback.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers ... The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode.'

verdicts.claim: FULL mode blocks (invoking the busy-handler) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent snapshot
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot ... new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE mode works like RESTART but also truncates the WAL log file to zero bytes just prior to successful return.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.'

verdicts.claim: By default, SQLite automatically checkpoints when the WAL file reaches 1000 pages, configurable via PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages (SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT ...)' and wal_autocheckpoint pragma; better-sqlite3 page does not mention the threshold.

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() requires an exclusive checkpoint lock; if another process is already checkpointing, SQLITE_BUSY is returned and no busy-handler
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.'

verdicts.claim: The automatic checkpointer only performs PASSIVE checkpoints, which may leave the WAL partially checkpointed if concurrent readers are active.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE' ... 'might not run to completion if there are concurrent readers or writers.'

verdicts.claim: After VACUUM in WAL mode, the rebuilt database is written to the WAL file (doubling disk consumption), and a separate checkpoint(TRUNCATE) call is required
verdicts.evidence: PhotoStructure: 'the entire rebuilt database gets written to the WAL file' ... 'you almost double disk consumption'; recommends PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE). better-sqlite3 page does not mention VACUUM.

verdicts.claim: SQLite WAL mode has a documented data race bug (the 'WAL-Reset bug' fixed in 2024 after 16 years) that can cause database corruption
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed a bug ... It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later.' Fix year is 2026, not 2024; verified-as-of 2024-09-01 tag is also impossible.

verdicts.claim: The WAL-Reset bug affects databases in WAL mode with two or more connections when those connections attempt to write or checkpoint at the same instant
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'only affects databases in WAL mode when there are two or more database connections open on the same file ... attempt to write or checkpoint at the same instant'; header field wrongly 'indicates that part of the WAL file has already been checkpointed, when in fact it has not been.'

verdicts.claim: The consensus.dev analysis notes that Tailscale hit the WAL-Reset bug because they checkpoint very aggressively with manual control
verdicts.evidence: theconsensus.dev returned HTTP 403 twice; Antithesis mentions Tailscale's outages but not aggressive checkpointing. Secondary coverage (WebSearch: Techzine/The Register) says Tailscale checkpointed manually and very aggressively, but the cited source could not be read.
